lens: Apple-inspired clarity — factual comprehension (simulated AI review lens)
reason: The inspected public experience has a strong proposition/action hierarchy, legible prose, restrained hairline structure and a purposeful engagement instrument that preserves Precision Instrument. The desktop and mobile hero captures make both audience actions easy to identify. Named past organizations are distinguished from unavailable approved case studies; applicant copy accurately distinguishes stripped written responses from identifying original resumes. I traced the implemented client journey from services and engagement terms to contact guidance, submission and feedback, and checked its supplied synthetic browser test/log. This supports local design quality, not observed factual comprehension or hosted delivery. Two bounded clarity/feedback improvements remain. The broad world-class claim and release readiness are unproven without integrated acceptance evidence; this is an independent AI assessment, not human or Apple endorsement.

findings.evidence: The hero identifies student-led consulting and practical recommendations but omits cost and engagement length. Those facts appear at lines 100-107 through SEMESTER_FACTS (src/lib/site-content.ts:158-163), after the organization figures and past-organization section. Both supplied hero captures confirm this hierarchy.
findings.userImpact: A first-time organization must scroll substantially or open another page to discover the central pro-bono, semester-long offer before deciding whether to inquire.
findings.suggestedFix: Include “pro-bono” and “semester-long” in the existing hero support sentence, preserving its concise hierarchy and current actions.

findings.evidence: submit converts a JSON parse failure to null, then treats every response.ok response as sent, resets the form and promises an email reply without checking result.ok. The actual route returns {ok:true} at src/app/api/contact/route.ts:52; tests/e2e/public-journeys.spec.ts:46-52 supplies only that valid synthetic receipt.
findings.userImpact: A malformed successful HTTP response would erase the inquiry and display an unjustified confirmation. This is a source-derived edge case, not an observed hosted failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Require the expected success receipt before resetting fields. Preserve the inquiry and explain that sending could not be confirmed when the receipt is missing or malformed; add a focused browser case for that response.
